claims: Batch outcomes expose nonnegative surplus, zero objective for unfilled outcomes, and deterministic `(volume, surplus)` AB extraction for filled outcomes.
The batch lexicographic objective is reflexive, transitive, total, and antisymmetric over `(volume, surplus)` pairs.
The AB addition operator is associative, commutative, and has `(0, 0)` as a left and right identity.
The canonical batch key has a checked component interpretation and every nonempty finite key set has a unique canonical minimum.
Batch approximation helpers preserve monotone total executed volume, order-independent total volume summation, and basic conservation facts.
Refinement steps are transitive and cannot degrade after two no-worse steps under the modeled better/no-worse relation.
proof_method: case analysis over filled/unfilled outcome constructors
lexicographic order decomposition over natural-number objective pairs
finite-set minimum existence and uniqueness under the canonical key order
list append and permutation-style summation arithmetic
relation algebra over strict improvement and no-worse refinement

checker_commands.command: cd lean-mathlib && lake build Proofs.BatchOptimality Proofs.BatchAuctionCanonical Proofs.BatchApproximation Proofs.BatchRefinementOrder
checker_commands.result: passed with pre-existing linter warnings in BatchAuctionCanonical
passed with pre-existing linter warnings in unrelated/imported proof files
passed for every definition and theorem listed in this receipt

boundaries: This receipt proves modeled batch objective, canonical key, approximation, and refinement-order facts only.
It does not prove runtime candidate generation completeness, pool execution correctness, user authorization, or cross-asset settlement safety.
The canonical-winner facts require the runtime and verifier to share the exact same total key and candidate set.
